hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a341a449700483900a5e0b9fc1fc0ab4.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{3\sin(2x - \pi) + 2}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin(2x)}$ is a horizontal shrink by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is shrunk from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin(2x)}$ to $\red{3\sin(2x)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $3$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $3$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over four, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over four, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over four, three).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{3\sin(2x)}$ to $\blue{3\sin(2x-\pi)+2}$, which is equivalent to $3\sin\left(2(x-\dfrac{\pi}{2})\right)+2$, is a translation to the right by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ units and a translation upwards by $2$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},2\right)$ and the maximum point is at $\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\pi,5\right)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (pi over two, two) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (three pi over four, five).
